releases.title: Applicant and checkride records, oral-only scenarios and checkride-order plans

items.text: Adding an applicant is now two steps: the applicant's details (including FTN), then a checkride with its date, test type, knowledge test and AKTR codes, IACRA application ID, instructor and school. The plan of action is built from the checkride.
Knowledge test results and AKTR codes are entered per checkride, and a plan only uses the codes from that checkride's test.
Organization admins can delete a checkride (optionally with its plan) or an applicant and all of their records.
The Setup step shows the applicant, checkride details, the knowledge test used and the AKTR codes, which you can change or reload from the checkride.
Only Oral tasks get a task scenario, one per task with no sub-scenarios. Flight tasks list their knowledge and risk questions and every skill to demonstrate.
Skill elements no longer get questions.

Appendix requirements tied to a task, such as the two non-precision approaches on VI.A, now appear under that task with a note box for how they will be met, on the plan, the printout and the test-day view.

The printed plan and the test-day view follow the checkride order: applicant and test information, pretest briefing, ground portion, preflight briefing, flight portion, postflight debriefing and closeout.

releases.title: Demonstration scenarios, per-element questions and appendix requirements

items.text: Task scenarios and sub-scenarios are now written so the applicant has to demonstrate the skill, and each one shows the element codes it covers.
Questions are now planned per element: every selected knowledge and risk element, plus each skill element, gets its own question and expected answer.
Choose 0, 1 or 2 questions per element, or Random. The second question is a follow-up that goes one step deeper on the first.
Skill elements get a question asked right after the sub-scenario where the applicant demonstrated it.
Approved bank questions are picked first; AI writes the rest and saves first questions to the bank as drafts for approval.

Eligibility and compliance now lists the appendix requirements from the ACS or PTS that apply to the test, with test-condition toggles (FSTD, inoperative equipment, no published VMC, limitation removal and more). They print on the plan and appear in the proof of compliance.

releases.title: Test timing, CFII, knowledge tests and AI scenarios

items.text: The plan button is now Start Test.
Debrief timing: Oral is now Ground, and both Ground and Flight are entered as HH:MM, for example 01:35.
Timers now count seconds and turn red with a blinking dot while running. Tap Stop to record the time; starting the flight timer stops the ground timer.
Hobbs start and Hobbs end fields for the flight portion. When both are entered, flight time fills in automatically. They print on the result and paper grade sheet.

Every new plan gets an AI scenario. The first time you open the Scenario step, smartPOA drafts the mission, then a scenario for every included task, oral tasks included. Each task scenario comes with two or three sub-scenarios that change one condition. Review and edit before finalizing.
All seeded question bank questions have been reviewed and approved.

Questions step: each task gets three questions, one easy (softball), one medium and one hard, each on a different element where possible. They come from your approved bank first, and AI fills only the levels the bank is missing. You can change the level of any question, pick again, or add your own.

Flight Instructor Instrument (CFII) plans now use FAA-S-8081-9E for airplane and helicopter. Required tasks follow the PTS Area of Operation notes for an initial rating, an add-on to a flight instructor or instrument instructor certificate, and renewal or reinstatement.

Applicants can have more than one knowledge test, for example FOI and FIA, with their own date, score, valid-until date and AKTR codes. Valid-until fills in from 61.39. New plans check the tests on file against the checkride and add every AKTR code.
Settings, Pre-test checklists: when a test type has no checklist, Draft with AI writes the endorsements and experience lists for you to check and save.
Clearer purpose names: Initial issuance (new certificate or rating) and Additional category or class (added to a certificate held), with a short explanation under the Purpose field.
Compliance quotes now cite FAA Order 8000.95E (issued September 15, 2026), which replaced 8000.95D. The quoted wording is unchanged. Thanks to Joe for the report.

Plans of action now leave out elements marked for another class of airplane, such as water rudders or water spray items on a land plan, or multiengine-only items on a single-engine plan. Those elements show greyed out with the class they belong to.
If an existing plan already has other-class elements, the Tasks step shows a warning with a button to remove them and their questions. Finalized plans need a revision first.

On the checkride debrief, tap "Standards, elements and questions" under any task to see its objective, references, the quoted ACS wording for each planned element, and the planned questions. Expand all opens every task at once.
When marking an element unsatisfactory, hold or hover on the code to see its ACS wording.

releases.title: Question bank filled from the ACS

items.text: The question bank now has a draft question and expected answer for every knowledge and risk management element in the Private, Commercial, Instrument, ATP and Flight Instructor ACS. They were written by AI in the same style as the previous POA program, so read each one before approving.
Filter the question bank by standard, area of operation, task, element type and status. After reading a task's drafts, approve them together with one button.
Approved bank questions that match the elements in a plan can be added from the plan's Questions step.

smartPOA now checks for new versions and updates itself, including on phones and home-screen installs. If you are in the middle of entering something, it waits and shows an Update button instead of interrupting you.
This window appears once after each update. You can reopen it anytime from What's new at the bottom of the menu.
You can add smartPOA to your phone's home screen for a full-screen, app-style view. On iPhone, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
Use the Feedback button in the top bar to report a problem, suggest a feature or ask a question. Replies appear under Your earlier feedback.
Feedback inbox under Administration lists every message, with status, replies and CSV export.
New Past checkrides tab with outcome totals, filters by year, applicant, certificate and result, attempt numbers and CSV export.

releases.title: Records from the previous POA program

items.text: Applicants, aircraft and checkride records from the previous plan of action program were brought into smartPOA.
Data Review tab lists records flagged for correction, plus automatic checks that clear once a record is fixed.
Checkride scheduling and outcome records, and AI-assisted scenario drafting that you review before use.
